requirement: Requirement and reference names MUST have nonempty dot-separated segments containing only ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. A `{req}` directive whose full name is invalid, including one whose chapter path gives an invalid namespace, and a role with an invalid name MUST remain literal and MUST NOT define or reference a requirement. For nested chapter paths, a leading `reqs/` and a final `index` or `README` segment MUST be omitted from the requirement namespace.
rationale:
The requirement is satisfied.

| Obligation | Implementation and verification |
|---|---|
| Names have nonempty dot-separated segments. | `src/lib.rs#fn[valid_name]` rejects an empty name and empty segments. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[invalid_names_remain_literal]` tests empty names, doubled dots, and leading/trailing dots. |
| Segments contain only ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. | `src/lib.rs#fn[valid_name]` checks every byte against exactly this set. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[invalid_names_remain_literal]` tests permitted letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, and rejects spaces, Unicode and other punctuation. |
| An invalid requirement directive remains literal. | `src/lib.rs#fn[definition_blocks]` excludes invalid local names; `src/lib.rs#fn[replace_definitions]` also checks the complete name before rendering. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[invalid_names_remain_literal]` verifies literal preservation. |
| An invalid directive does not define a requirement. | `src/lib.rs#fn[preprocess_book]` excludes invalid complete names from its definition map; `src/evidence.rs#fn[collect_definitions]` likewise declines to insert them. Parser rejection of invalid local names is tested in `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[invalid_names_remain_literal]`. |
| These protections include invalid namespaces supplied by chapter paths. | Both definition collectors validate the result of `src/lib.rs#fn[full_requirement_name]`. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[chapters_with_invalid_namespaces_define_nothing_in_the_book]` verifies unchanged directive/reference text and absence of generated detail pages. `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[invalid_full_names_from_chapter_paths_are_reported_and_not_defined]` verifies rejection and absence of an evidence obligation for the invalid name. |
| A role with an invalid name remains literal. | `src/lib.rs#fn[reference_roles]` and `src/fenced.rs#fn[opening_fence]` reject invalid names. The rendering functions preserve text not recognized as a reference. Inline rejection is tested in `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[invalid_names_remain_literal]`; literal rendered output is also checked by `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[chapters_with_invalid_namespaces_define_nothing_in_the_book]`. Fenced rejection is tested in `src/fenced.rs#mod[tests]/fn[opening_fences_take_a_role_and_one_valid_or_built_in_name]`. |
| An invalid role does not reference a requirement. | The same parsers return no reference for invalid names; the inline and fenced parser tests above assert that outcome directly. |
| Nested paths omit a leading `reqs/`. | `src/lib.rs#fn[chapter_namespace]` removes this component only for nested paths. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[chapter_path_prefixes_the_requirement_name]` tests removal, a nonleading `reqs`, and the unnested boundary. `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines]` also verifies collection under the resulting namespace. |
| Nested paths omit a final `index`. | The same function and namespace test cover nested `index`, combined prefix/suffix removal, an empty resulting namespace, and unnested `index`. The evidence invalid-path test additionally checks `reqs/index.md`. |
| Nested paths omit a final `README`. | The same function removes `README`, and `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[chapter_path_prefixes_the_requirement_name]` explicitly asserts this result. |

These helpers are reachable from the marked implementation roots: `preprocess_book` reaches namespace construction, definition parsing/rendering and reference rendering; `collect_definitions` reaches namespace construction, definition parsing and complete-name validation. The tests listed carry references to `requirements.ci.identifiers`.

The special recognition of `habeas:<name>` is specified by `requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, which the relevant implementation also marks; it is not an unspecified extension to project requirement names. No unacknowledged gap was found.

text: Requirement and reference names MUST have nonempty dot-separated segments containing only ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. A `{req}` directive whose full name is invalid, including one whose chapter path gives an invalid namespace, and a role with an invalid name MUST remain literal and MUST NOT define or reference a requirement. For nested chapter paths, a leading `reqs/` and a final `index` or `README` segment MUST be omitted from the requirement namespace.
Habeas MUST provide built-in definitions named `habeas:<name>`, available in
every project without a declaration. Each built-in MUST have fixed text, which
states its obligations and is documented in Habeas's reference documentation, and
MUST state which reference roles may use it. References MUST resolve built-in
names alongside project definitions. So that every book stands alone, the book
MUST render a reference to a built-in as a badge without a link whose hover text
gives the built-in's full text. Built-ins MUST NOT require or permit evidence
files and MUST NOT appear in the requirements index, `habeas status`, or the
missing-evidence check of {cite}`requirements.ci.coverage`. A project definition
MUST NOT use a full name beginning with `habeas:`; validation MUST report one,
and the `:` character already makes such names invalid under
{cite}`requirements.ci.identifiers`. Validation MUST report a reference to a
